Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas · Money, work & business

provide for verb

support; see to someone’s needs

also support a family, make provision for, see to it, maintain, keep a family

classical

Cic. Att. 11.3.3: cūrā et prōvidē nē quid eī dēsit
Caes. BG 5.8: reī frūmentāriae (Lewis & Short)

prōvideō, prōvidēre, prōvīdī, prōvīsum

verb, second conjugation, with the dative, or nē or ut

see to, make provision for

Of seeing to it in advance that someone has what they need.

Examples

  • studeat parāre ea, quae suppeditent ad cultum et ad victum, nec sibi sōlī, sed conjugī, līberīs cēterīsque, quōs cārōs habeat tuērīque dēbeat

    he strives to get what will provide clothing and food, not for himself alone but for his wife, his children and the others he holds dear and is bound to look afterCic. Off. 1.12

  • omnibus rēbus cūrā et prōvidē nē quid eī dēsit

    take every care and see to it that she lacks nothingCic. Att. 11.3.3

  • Neque iners, alit illās: sōlus omnem familiam sustentat

    and he’s no idler: he keeps them; he alone supports the whole householdTer. Ad. 481–482

Other words

  • tueor, tuērī, tuitus sum — look after, keep

    verb, second conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.12: quōs cārōs habeat tuērīque dēbeat

    Classically to look at, and above all to look after, maintain and protect (Lewis & Short).

  • sustentō, sustentāre, sustentāvī, sustentātum — support, keep (with money or food)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Ter. Ad. 481–482: sōlus omnem familiam sustentat

    Of keeping a household. In composed Latin, “his family” is suī or domus: familia is the whole household.

  • alō, alere, aluī, altum (alitum) — feed, keep

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Liv. 21.33.11: per trīduum exercitum aluit

    Of feeding and keeping people or animals.

See also provide, take care.

SourcesLewis & Short: provideo · Lewis & Short: tueor · Lewis & Short: sustento · Lewis & Short: alo
